metadata.title: Ryan Miller quiet in Week 3
metadata.description: Ryan Miller caught two of his three targets for 15 yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Miller has seen minimal involvement in the Miami offense to begin the season, recording three targets or less in each of the first three contests. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Cleared to play Sunday
metadata.description: Miller (hip/back) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Miller was questionable ahead of the meeting with Kansas City due to hip and back injuries. However, the wideout is good to go. With Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out, Miller, who had a touchdown in Week 2 against the 49ers, could be more involved.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller Could Earn More Time
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Ryan Miller only played seven offensive snaps in Week 2 against the 49ers, mostly after the game was decided. He did deliver one of the team's biggest plays of the season, though, by catching his only target for a 77-yard touchdown strike from Malik Willis. That was Willis's only passing touchdown of the season in the first two weeks, and Miller will look to turn that success into more opportunities going forward. The fourth-year receiver from Furman is officially listed as questionable for Week 3 with a hip injury, but he got in a full practice on Friday, which usually indicates he'll be able to suit up. Miller could get more time at WR with Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out and Chris Bell (knee) still working his way back from offseason surgery. He's in a tough matchup against the Chiefs and working in a struggling offense, so he isn't a good option to start for fantasy this week, falling outside the RotoBaller WR rankings. It will be interesting to see if he earns more time, though, since the Dolphins' offense is desperately looking for the potential for big plays like the one he delivered last week. He has the potential to emerge as a deep-league pickup if he is in a bigger role this week.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Miller (hip) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Miller was limited in Wednesday's practice before missing Thursday's session. The wide receiver ultimately upgraded to full participation in Friday's session, making it likely that Miller will be able to suit up as a depth option for Sunday's contest.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller (hip/back) officially questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Ryan Miller (hip/back) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Kanas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Miller is uncertain to play on Sunday. He's dealing with a pair of injuries right now and is likely considered day-to-day as a result. If he's cleared to play, he will see more work than usual with Caleb Douglas (ankle) set to be sidelined against the Chiefs.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Misses practice Thursday
metadata.analysis: Miller opened the week by practicing in a limited capacity, but he wasn't out there Thursday, which isn't an encouraging sign regarding his availability for the Week 3 meeting with the Chiefs. Miller logged only seven offensive snaps in the 35-13 loss to the 49ers in Week 2. However, with Chris Bell (knee) and Caleb Douglas (ankle) also battling injuries, there's a path for more playing time for Miller on Sunday, depending on who is available.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Dealing with hip issue
metadata.description: Miller (hip/back) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: It's not clear when Miller suffered the injury, but his availability for Week 3 is now in  doubt. If he's not able to practice in full Thursday or Friday, there's a good chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Catches long TD in Week 2 defeat
metadata.description: Miller caught his only target for a 77-yard touchdown Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Miller worked mostly on special teams during the contest, but he got a chance to play seven offensive snaps. The fourth-year wideout made the most of the opportunity, connecting with QB Malik Willis on a 77-yard score late in the fourth quarter. The game was out of reach for Miami at that point, but it was still a significant moment for Miller as he tries to earn more playing time on offense. The door could be open a crack for that, as Caleb Douglas hurt his ankle Sunday and is uncertain to be able to play Week 3. With that in mind, Miller is buried pretty deep on Miami's WR depth chart, so he's not guaranteed to see the field often even if Douglas is ruled out.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller hauls in long touchdown late in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Ryan Miller caught his only target for a 77-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Miller is not a player to suddenly target on the waiver wire. He only played seven snaps Sunday, with his one big play coming when the Dolphins were down 35-6 late in the fourth quarter. The third-year pro was picked up late in the preseason by the Dolphins to add depth at wide receiver.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller claimed off waivers by Dolphins
metadata.description: The Dolphins claimed WR Ryan Miller off waivers.
metadata.analysis: Miller was waived by the Giants earlier in the week. He'll add depth in the wide receiver room for Miami.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Claimed by Miami
metadata.description: The Dolphins claimed Miller off waivers from the Giants on Tuesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Miller was competing for a roster spot with the Giants, but it appears the wide receiver was not as close to a depth option as he had hoped. The 26-year-old now has a chance to compete in a wide-open corps, with Friday's preseason finale against the Falcons likely holding a lot of sway over the final decisions for cutdown day.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller waived by Giants
metadata.description: The Giants waived WR Ryan Miller.
metadata.analysis: Miller will figure to seek another opportunity during training camp.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Cut loose by Giants
metadata.description: Miller was waived by the Giants on Monday. Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Miller was brought in this spring before the 2026 Draft and had been working to earn a roster spot. However, with final cutdowns looming, the Giants have opted to go in a different direction and Miller is now subject to waivers.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Officially re-signed by G-Men
metadata.description: The Giants re-signed Miller on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: The 26-year-old wideout logged 13 regular-season appearances with Tampa Bay in 2025, securing two of four targets for 34 yards and a score. Miller had been claimed off waivers by the Giants in December and tendered as an exclusive rights free agent.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Joining Big Blue
metadata.description: Miller is slated to sign with the Giants, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The 26-year-old wideout from Furman appeared in 13 games for the Buccaneers in 2025, catching two of four targets for 34 yards and a touchdown across 328 total snaps (205 on special teams, 123 on offense). Following his deal with the Giants, Miller will likely compete for a depth spot in New York's wide receiver room ahead of the 2026 season.

metadata.title: Ryan Miller - Not playing Sunday
metadata.description: Miller (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's Week 18 matchup versus Dallas, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: The Giants claimed Miller off waivers from Tampa Bay on Dec. 11, but they won't end up deploying him for any game action. The third-year wideout will finish the campaign having played in 13 contests (all with the Buccaneers), tallying two catches on four targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. Of Miller's 14 career NFL catches, three have gone for a score.
